stage: Stage 0 read-only audit, no GPU execution

header_fields.name: ARRIVE_AT_LATCH_ID
header_fields.meaning: ID of the latch this QMD arrives at when the program's pre-exit fires
header_fields.evidence: header field present in NVCEC0_QMDV05_00/05_01; written by tinygrad/runtime/ops_nv.py:49

header_fields.name: WAIT_ON_LATCH_ID
header_fields.meaning: ID of the latch this QMD waits on before its grid launches
header_fields.evidence: header field present; written by tinygrad/runtime/ops_nv.py:51

header_fields.name: ARRIVE_AT_LATCH_VALID
header_fields.evidence: header field present; device probe phase_c_native_qmd_latch_4.json:17

header_fields.name: WAIT_ON_LATCH_VALID
header_fields.evidence: header field present; device probe phase_c_native_qmd_latch_4.json consumer_latch_fields

header_fields.name: LATCH_RELEASE_INVALIDATE_ENABLE
header_fields.meaning: invalidate caches when the latch is released/acquired
header_fields.evidence: header field present; no semantic documentation and no device exercise in this repo

header_fields.name: ENABLE_PROGRAM_PRE_EXIT

capability_questions.question: How many latch IDs are usable on sm_120?
capability_questions.evidence: ID fields are 32-bit, but no public header/doc gives a latch pool size; phase_c only proved ID 7 on one pair
capability_questions.required_probe: Stage 2 synthetic sweep: same consecutive pair with distinct latch IDs, record checksum and overlap

capability_questions.question: Can one consumer wait on more than one latch?
capability_questions.evidence: QMD has a single WAIT_ON_LATCH_ID field and no multiple-wait field; public headers contain no multiple-wait description

capability_questions.question: Can multiple producers arrive at the same latch ID?
capability_questions.evidence: not stated in the public header; do not infer aggregation semantics
capability_questions.required_probe: Stage 2 synthetic multi-producer probe with checksums

capability_questions.question: Can a latch arm a non-consecutive same-queue QMD pair?
capability_questions.evidence: no documented arming rule; the only device evidence is a consecutive pair (phase_c_native_qmd_latch_4.json)
capability_questions.required_probe: Stage 2 synthetic A-B-C chain with A->C arming

capability_questions.question: Is latch state safe across graph replay, flush, and the five replay groups?
capability_questions.evidence: no reuse/reset semantics in the public header; no device evidence across replay boundaries
capability_questions.required_probe: Stage 2 synthetic replay/flush bracket before any production arm

capability_questions.question: Does QMD pre-exit at last CTA launch guarantee producer data is visible to the consumer?
capability_questions.evidence: pre-exit-at-last-CTA is the launch gate; CUDA PDL guide requires a consumer grid-dependency wait/fence before dependent access; native wait placement is currently at instruction zero and has not been proven data-safe
capability_questions.required_probe: Stage 2 native candidate with wait after producer trigger and checksums; Stage 3 real-route wait-exit timestamps

device_proven_facts.fact: latch ID 7 with arrive/wait/pre-exit fields produces overlap on a same-queue consecutive pair
device_proven_facts.evidence: phase_c_native_qmd_latch_4.json: median overlap_us 99.808, wall_us 463.488, checksum_correct_all true
device_proven_facts.note: this is a matched synthetic grid, not the real decode route

device_proven_facts.fact: renderer-side native PDL (griddepcontrol.wait + launch_dependents) also overlaps
device_proven_facts.note: the QMD-latch arm has no renderer wait instruction, so its consumer-grid gate is purely the QMD fields

policy_consequences.closed_default: until the four named-unavailable capability rows are measured, unsafe cases fall back to the existing full-completion dependency
policy_consequences.no_inference: pool size, multi-wait, same-latch aggregation, non-consecutive arming, and replay safety must not be inferred from CUDA driver semantics
policy_consequences.alias_authority: typed edges still require span-level alias adjudication; this audit does not grant alias safety
